req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. The violation was in test[5]: kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is a structural/positive heuristic that traces valid state transitions; it must be paired with kind=positive. The fix changes test[5] kind from 'negative' to 'positive' because the test exercises a valid state transition sequence (login -> logout -> delete) and verifies the system correctly redirects, which is the expected positive behaviour of the login_required guard after a state change. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_anonymous_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with a fresh test database containing pre-loaded rows
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
Post id 1 exists in the database (author_id=5)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: anonymous POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_authenticated_author_delete_succeeds_not_redirected_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with a fresh test database containing pre-loaded rows
Post id 2 exists and belongs to Rahul (author_id=1)
expected: Location header after delete is / (blog index), NOT /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-014: redirect to /auth/login must NOT occur for authenticated users
Confirms the login_required decorator only blocks anonymous users
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302
assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
delete_r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert delete_r.status_code == 302
assert delete_r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'
assert delete_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
